subject: estimates for standardized solution in a multigroup confirmatory factor analysis

messages.author: bbfbdc76ffaf4909
messages.subject: estimates for standardized solution in a multigroup confirmatory factor analysis
parts:
Dear all,

A quick question about obtaining standardized solutions for MGCFA models.

I have run a multi-group (2 countries, in my case) CFA on a 2-factor measurement scale. In my analysis, I have constrained the intercepts and loadings to be equal across groups. The model fit is fine, and the estimated (unstandardized) intercepts and loadings are indeed equivalent across groups.

However, my co-authors and I would like to report the standardized solution (the column "Std.all" in the output) and I notice that these are not identical across groups. There is clearly something I'm not understanding about the way the standardized estimates are computed.

Can anyone provide some insight as to why the standardized solution (but not the non-standardized solution) differs across groups? It seems that, if I can't report the standardized solution, I'd be better off to provide the non-standardized estimates.

I'm pasting below a reproducible example using the Holzinger Swineford data that comes with the lavaan package. Running this model gives the the same situation as running the model on my own data- the non-standardized loadings and intercepts are identical across groups, but the standardized solutions are different across groups.


HS.model <- ' visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3
textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
speed =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '

fit <-  cfa(HS.model,
 data = HolzingerSwineford1939,
 group = "school",
 group.equal=c("loadings", "intercepts"))

summary(fit, fit.measures=TRUE, standardized=TRUE)


Many thanks in advance for any insight that anyone could provide.

Best,
M Friedman

messages.author: 71bfb5f1e96782a8
messages.subject: Re: estimates for standardized solution in a multigroup confirmatory factor analysis
parts: the standardized loadings are the unstandardized loadings divided by the variances of the latent and observed variables. unless you constrain the variances across groups, the standardized loadings might be different between groups.

messages.author: bbfbdc76ffaf4909
messages.subject: Re: estimates for standardized solution in a multigroup confirmatory factor analysis
parts:
Hi Hans,

Many thanks for your prompt and helpful reply. This makes perfect sense.

I could constrain the variances across groups in order to obtain the standardized loadings, but that would be evaluating a fundamentally different model than the one I've been looking at.

In my case, I'm thinking it makes more sense to keep the model the same and report the unstandardized loadings.

Thanks very much for the clarification.

Best,
MF
